Definition: from the same as G3694 (through the idea of backwardness); (adverbially) late in the day; by extension, after the close of the day:--(at) even, in the end.
BiblicalUsage: Late in the day, or at the end, is how this word works. Mark says when even was come, Jesus went out of the city to Bethany, and Matthew says in the end of the Sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, the women came to see the sepulchre.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe evening is when the day's work is counted: Jesus went out to Bethany when evening came, and the Sabbath ended to find the tomb empty.
